source.title: Shared Global and Local Geometry of Language Model Embeddings
source.authors: Andrew Lee; M. Weber; Fernanda Viégas; M. Wattenberg

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarity of token-embedding geometry across differently sized language models, using Pearson correlations, LLE-weight similarity, and intrinsic-dimension correlations. These are conceptual tests of representational convergence, not the original study’s full cross-modal or broad-scale design.
record.gate_note: The paper tests within-family language-model geometry, local-geometry measures, and linear transfer of steering vectors. It does not test paired image-caption alignment, convergence across random seeds, or recurrence of universal features. Semantic-coherence versus intrinsic-dimension results are not rows because they do not measure cross-model convergence. Cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-model similarity of token (un)embedding geometry within the GPT2, Llama3 and Gemma2 families using global, LLE and intrinsic-dimension measures, plus one cross-data pair. It also transfers steering vectors between models through a least-squares linear map. These bear on V4, V6 and V7. It does not analyse how alignment changes with scale or capability, so V1 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two qualifications. The authors conclude that token embeddings within a model family usually share global orientation and local geometry (LLE, intrinsic dimension). For untied Llama3 models this holds for the unembeddings but not the input embeddings. Gemma2 shows weaker global similarity and low local (ID) similarity. They speculate training data drives the similarity, citing one cross-data pair at 0.32. A least-squares linear map transfers steering vectors between different-size models in most cases.
record.recipe_differences: Measures token-embedding and unembedding geometry within GPT2, Llama3, and Gemma2 families using cosine-matrix correlations, LLE weights, and intrinsic-dimension correlations; it also tests linear-map transfer of steering vectors. This is not a broad cross-modal alignment or scale-and-capability study.
record.method_sensitivity: Findings vary across geometric measures and embedding versus unembedding spaces. Intrinsic-dimension similarity is high for many GPT2 pairs but weak or negative for Gemma2 pairs; the reported global geometry also differs between untied Llama3 input embedding and unembedding spaces.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a model, tokens with lower intrinsic dimension have more semantically coherent ConceptNet neighbourhoods. Spearman is -0.67 for GPT2-M and -0.45 for Llama3-3B, but 0.22 for Gemma2-2B and fades toward zero as k grows (Tables 2, 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low local intrinsic dimension of token embeddings marks semantically coherent clusters.

fits_no_version.finding: Llama3 base and instruction-tuned models have a global embedding-geometry correlation of about 1.00.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction tuning leaves token-embedding geometry essentially unchanged.

record.problems: The main geometry comparisons are within model families sharing tokenizers, and model capability is not measured. The different-training-data comparison is a single pair and does not isolate training data as the cause. Several LLE and steering-transfer results are presented in figures without numerical summaries in the text. Intrinsic-dimension comparisons use N=500 tokens.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted due to the row limit. Pairwise Llama3 numeric matrix entries are not separately extracted where the flattened figure layout does not make the pairwise assignment unambiguous; the paper's explicit aggregate descriptions are recorded in r10-r11.

untested.parts: No analysis of alignment as a function of model size or capability. No comparison across architectures, objectives or modalities. Within-family models share a tokenizer and probably data.
No vision–language or paired image–caption experiment.
No comparison of models trained from different random seeds.
Stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping are not tested. There is no quantified loss of the linear map, and no transfer across families or tokenizers.
No comparison of neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Neighbour count k and the variance threshold are not varied for the cross-model LLE and ID comparisons. There are no out-of-distribution inputs, and token sampling is not varied.
No plateau analysis. The effect of data is not isolated from architecture, size or tokenizer-training differences.

missing.what: Llama3 intrinsic-dimension cross-model correlations: embeddings 0.43–0.95 (e.g. 1B–8B 0.43, 8B–11B-V 0.97); unembeddings 0.50–0.99.
Steering transfer into Llama3-3B from 1B and 8B across seven behaviours.
Nearest-neighbour tokens of transferred steering vectors match those of the originals (e.g. myopic, toxicity).
Tokens with zero LLE similarity across models, attributed to undertrained tokens. Recall against Land & Bartolo's list is 0.415 for Llama3-8B and 0.11 for GPT2-M.

record.verdict_notes: V1 links were removed from r1–r11 because the study never relates alignment to scale or capability, and all main comparisons are within families that share a tokenizer. For V6 rows, the state is recast to mean whether the conclusion changes across measures or spaces, rather than the level of alignment. Steering results (r25–r29) are figure-only. The paper's claim that alignment persists in hidden layers is an inference from the unembeddings, not a measurement.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure capability or performance, convergence across different architectures/objectives/modalities broadly, or convergence across independently trained models outside the tested families.
No paired images and captions or vision-language representation alignment experiment.
No comparison of models trained from different random initializations.

Tests a learned linear map between unembedding spaces using 100,000 corresponding token vectors, then transfers steering vectors. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or transfer without paired data.
No systematic comparison of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.
Tests several geometric measures on the reported models and token sets, but does not systematically vary the input data distribution or test out-of-distribution convergence.
Compares one pair trained on different datasets and speculates about training data; does not isolate data from other training differences or quantify a convergence plateau.
